1971 War crimes: 70-yr-old fugitive convict arrested from a city slum
2023-03-01T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/crime-justice/news/1971-war-crimes-70-yr-old-fugitive-convict-arrested-city-slum-3259891

The Rab yesterday arrested a 70-year-old fugitive convict of war crimes from a slum in the capital's Demra area.

The arrestee, Abu Muslim Mohammad Ali, from Gaibandha's Sundarganj upazila, was sentenced to death by the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT-1) for committing crimes against humanity during the Liberation War.

He had been hiding in the slum, maintaining a low profile.

Acting on a tip-off, a Rab-3 team arrested Abu Muslim on Saturday midnight, according to a press release signed by Lt Col Arif Mohiuddin Ahmed, commanding officer of Rab-3.

Abu Muslim was one of the organisers of Jamaat-e-Islami's student wing Islami Chhatra Sangha in 1971, and an active member of Sundarganj Thana Jamaat-e-Islami, said the release.

He was also an active member of the Peace Committee and was involved in various criminal activities, including looting, in Gaibandha's Kamarjani area.

According to Rab sources, on October 9, 1971, due to previous enmity, local Peace Committee members, led by Abdur Rahim and Abu Muslim, along with members of the Pakistani army, attacked, looted and burned down the house of Ganesh Chandra Barman in Malibari village.

They then brutally tortured and killed Ganesh and his friend Akbar Ali. In 2013, Anisur Rahman, the son of Akbar Ali, filed a case against Abu Muslim.

In 2014, the case was transferred to the International Criminal Tribunal, which sentenced him to death in 2017, the release added.

According to the Rab, Abu Muslim was holed up in his relative's house in Sundarganj from 2013 to 2015.

When an arrest warrant was issued in 2015, he went into hiding in Belkar Char, located on the banks of the Teesta River, where he earned a living as a day labourer.

Later in 2021, he fled to Dhaka and started living in a rented house in Savar's Ashulia area. He worked as a day labourer there as well, before becoming a home tutor.

In hiding, he used pseudonyms to keep his identity hidden.

Fearing arrest, he had been staying in the slum in Demra area since January, the release added.
